articles.title: Kolkata Pandal Tragedy: 7 Arrested After 19 Deaths, Amit Shah Cancels Political Events
articles.description: A devastating tragedy at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata has claimed 19 lives and left around 25 people injured, triggering swift action by the police and administration. Following the incident, Kolkata Police registered a suo motu case and arrested seven people allegedly linked to the event's organisation. Those arrested reportedly include the committee's vice-president and the security in-charge. Authorities have also constituted a fact-finding committee and a Special Task Force (STF) to investigate the circumstances that led to the deadly incident. According to preliminary reports, heavy rainfall and an unusually large crowd contributed to chaotic scenes near the pandal's exit gate. Panic reportedly broke out as people attempted to leave, resulting in a stampede-like situation. Several families were devastated as visitors who had arrived to seek Goddess Durga's blessings never returned home. The exit gate has been sealed to preserve the crime scene and facilitate a detailed investigation. Kolkata Police Commissioner has also ordered restrictions under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in parts of the affected area from October 18 to October 20. The restrictions aim to prevent large gatherings and ensure that the investigation proceeds without disruption, amid concerns about possible demonstrations. Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who is visiting Kolkata, cancelled his scheduled political programmes following the tragedy. He visited a hospital to meet the injured and review the situation. Visuals from the hospital showed the Home Minister interacting with those receiving treatment. The administration is now under pressure to establish the exact sequence of events, determine whether safety arrangements were adequate and identify those responsible.

articles.title: Escalation In Middle East As Iran Hits Kurdish Bases In Erbil; Blast Hits Iraqi Militia HQ
articles.description: Iran has reportedly launched another drone strike against an Iranian Kurdish opposition group based in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region. Drones targeted a Komala Party base in Balisan, Erbil province, damaging buildings but causing no reported casualties. The attack follows a separate drone strike on a camp belonging to the Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran (KDPI) in Koya district. Since the US-Israeli war against Iran began on February 28, more than 1,000 drones and missiles have reportedly targeted the Kurdistan Region, launched by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and Iran-backed Iraqi militias. Meanwhile, clashes between Iranian forces and Kurdish fighters have intensified in western Iran, adding to regional tensions as Tehran faces mounting military and security pressures.
